To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NO is not toxic to plants, and that NO and H2O2 are required to activate the hypersensitive response, which is an important component of the plant disease resistance response.
NO and ROIs play key roles in triggering disease resistance in soybean cells and that the balance of these two signals determines whether or not the hypersensitive cell death response is activated.
NO and ROIs play a crucial role for the activation of hypersensitive cell-death in plants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of reactive oxygen intermediates and nitric oxide in the activation of the hypersensitive disease response in soybean and other plants.
the role of nitric oxide (NO), reactive oxygen intermediates and the plant hypersensitive response (a form of programmed cell death).

understanding the role of reactive oxygen intermediates and nitric oxide in plant defense mechanisms against pathogens and the role of these compounds in cell death and programmed cell death in plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
in soybean NO and ROIs are required for the HR, but NO is not sufficient to kill cells, and NO is not toxic when O2 levels are high.
the plant and animal immune systems use the same signals (NO and ROIs) to trigger cell death.
in soybean, NO cooperates with O2 to trigger cell death, and O2 is converted into H2O2 by the action of superoxide dismutases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NO and ROI signaling are integrated during the HR in plants.
the hypersensitive disease resistance mechanism of plants is a NO/H2O 2 dependent process.
in plants the hypersensitive response is activated by NO and H2O2 cooperation whereas in animals NO and ROIs cooperate to trigger cytotoxic events.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NO cooperates with H2O in triggering cell death, and this cooperation is mediated through NO scavenging of O2.
NO is not a mediator for oxidative cell death.
the plant HR differs from the animal immune response in the way that NO is used.
